summary: ASED shows a clear, consistent, statistically significant improvement over degree-only SED on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day. Global CRPS improves by 2.92% (passes the 1% threshold). Extra-tropics CRPS improves by 0.75% (narrowly misses the 1% threshold but is outside the noise range). The method captures real directional error structure (anisotropy ratio 4.26) and works as hypothesized.
analysis: Core comparison (ASED vs SED): CRPS global 139.60 vs 143.80 (delta=2.92%, PASS). CRPS extratropics 181.54 vs 182.90 (delta=0.75%, FAIL strict threshold). Both improvements are outside SED mean+/-std (non-overlapping), indicating statistically significant gains across all 5 seeds. ASED also outperforms isotropic GP baseline (143.47 global, 182.94 extratropics), confirming that within-degree anisotropy structure adds value beyond both degree-only spectral and isotropic spatial correlation approaches. All methods substantially outperform deterministic baseline (160.93 global), confirming ensemble value. IFS-ENS (117.34 global) remains the best reference. Spread-skill ratios: ASED achieves the best global SSR (1.123) among ML methods, and near-perfect extratropical calibration (1.010). Calibration anisotropy w-ratio is 4.26 (>>0.1), confirming substantial directional error structure exists in GraphCast residuals, especially at synoptic scales (ratio 5.99).
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) Both main experiment and all baselines ran successfully and produced results. (2) ASED shows a clear positive signal with 2.92% global CRPS improvement over SED, strongly passing the 1% threshold. (3) Extra-tropics improvement (0.75%) is real and consistent across all 5 seeds (outside noise range) but narrowly misses the strict 1% threshold. (4) The improvement is physically interpretable -- synoptic-scale anisotropy ratio of 5.99 aligns with expected storm-track directional error structure. (5) Per evaluation guidelines, since there is a clear positive signal (strong global improvement + consistent sub-threshold extratropical improvement), the approach is promising and worth further analysis. The strict criterion is partially met, not fully refuted.
